---
name: factory-review
description: First-pass code review of this branch against its base (correctness, tests, readability, security, scope), with findings ranked by severity. Uses Claude Code's built-in code-review when it is available, otherwise the factory-kit code-reviewer agent, and adds the built-in security-review when the change is security-sensitive. Use before committing or opening a pull request.
argument-hint: "[--base <branch>] [--fix] [--reviewer builtin|agent] [--effort low|medium|high] [--security auto|always|never]"
---

<!-- Generated by sync-kit from factory-kit 0.15.0. Edit plugins/factory-kit in solo-factory, not this copy. -->

Review the current change set. Arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

1. Resolve the base: `--base` argument, else the MR target in `CLAUDE.md`, else `origin`'s default
   branch. Run `git diff --stat origin/<base>...HEAD` and `git diff --stat HEAD`; if both are empty,
   say there is nothing to review and stop.
2. **Pick the reviewer**, and say which one you used:
   - **Built-in `code-review`** (the default when it's available): use it if a skill named
     `code-review` (no plugin prefix) is in your list of available skills and the arguments don't
     say `--reviewer agent`. Invoke it with the Skill tool and the args
     `<effort> origin/<base>...HEAD`, where `<effort>` is the `--effort` argument or `medium`. If
     it rejects that target form, call it with just the effort; with no target it reviews the
     current diff. Never pass `ultra`: that starts a billed cloud review, which only the user can
     start. Never pass `--comment`, `--fix` or `--post`; this skill applies fixes itself in step 5.
     When it reports findings through a findings tool or its own format, read them from there.
   - **factory-kit `code-reviewer` agent**: use it when `code-review` isn't available, when it fails,
     or with `--reviewer agent`. Launch `factory-code-reviewer` with the Agent tool, passing the
     base ref.
   - The built-in review checks correctness. The agent also covers tests, readability, security
     and scope creep. If the built-in reviewer ran, also check the diff yourself for those, briefly:
     new behavior without a test, secrets or unsafe input handling, and changes unrelated to the
     branch's purpose.
   **Security pass** (`--security`, default `auto`): with `always`, or with `auto` when the change
   is security-sensitive, also run a security review. The change is security-sensitive when either
   of these holds:
   - the diff touches sign-in, sessions or tokens, permission checks, cryptography, raw SQL, input
     parsing or validation at a boundary, file uploads, CORS or headers, secrets and env handling,
     or adds or upgrades a dependency;
   - the spec (`docs/specs/<N>.md`) has `[security]` criteria.

   Use Claude Code's built-in `security-review` skill if it is in your list of available skills.
   Invoke it with the Skill tool and no arguments, and don't pass any flag that posts comments. If
   it isn't available, launch the `factory-code-reviewer` agent again and tell it to look only
   at security. Say which one ran, or why none did. Check that every `[security]` criterion has a
   test in the diff; a missing one is a `major` finding. Security findings go into the same table,
   and an exploitable one is a `blocker`.
3. Spot-check the findings before showing them: open each `blocker` and `major` location (or each
   finding the built-in review marks as confirmed or high severity) and drop anything that is
   wrong on inspection. Say how many you dropped.
4. Show the findings as one table (severity, `path:line`, issue, suggested fix), most severe first,
   whichever reviewer produced them. Map the built-in review's levels onto `blocker` / `major` /
   `minor` / `nit`.
5. With `--fix`, apply the fixes for `blocker` and `major` findings, then re-run the relevant
   tests. Without it, ask which findings to fix.
6. If the diff is large (more than ~500 changed lines) or touches auth, payments, data migrations,
   or secrets, recommend also running `/code-review ultra` (a deeper, billed cloud review the user
   starts) and a human review. This skill is a first pass, not a replacement.
